debate: Will

I suggest we go around in order and each share any gut instinct or ask one quick question—no hard evidence needed, just initial impressions. I’ll start: right now I don’t have a strong suspicion but I’m watching how everyone handles this first spotlight. Next up is Sam—what’s your instinct or question?
Mason

Thanks, Will. I don’t have any strong suspicions yet—I’m paying attention to how much detail and hesitation everyone shows. One quick question for you: when you say you’re watching how people handle this first spotlight, what specific behaviors or cues are you looking for?
Jackson

I like Will’s idea of sharing gut instincts and Mason’s focus on detail. Let’s build on that: we each ask one quick question to the next player to see how they handle the spotlight. Sam, what’s one specific behavior you’d look for to spot a Werewolf? After Sam answers, I’ll turn to Hayley. Sound good?
Bert

Jackson, I see the logic in your chain, but sometimes the smoothest strategies come from the Wolves. Will’s opening was almost too polished, and Mason’s focus on hesitation feels pretty textbook. Let’s shake things up—Scott, what’s your gut instinct so far, and has anyone’s early play struck you as a bit too rehearsed?
Sam

I’d watch for someone who abruptly changes their story or overcorrects when probed—like someone saying “I have no suspicions” and then laying out an elaborate theory moments later. Mason, you’ve been zeroing in on hesitation, but aren’t you just swapping one gut feeling for another by second-guessing Will’s polished opening? Scott, before we dive deeper, whose shifting narratives strike you as most convenient—and who really gains by throwing around labels like “textbook” so early?
Hayley

Sam makes a solid point about shifting narratives—but I can’t shake how polished Will’s opening was, or how Jackson’s chain-of-questions feels too orchestrated. Feels like they’re running the show together. Scott, do you see any signs that Will and Jackson might be coordinating to steer the debate?
Scott

I’m concerned by how smoothly Will and Jackson are running this “chain” of questions—smooth coordination can be a Werewolf tactic. Let’s switch it up. Will, you go first: without a formula, name one specific cue you’d actually act on if you saw it tonight. Then Jackson, do the same. After that, I want Hayley and Sam to each ask one off-the-cuff question to Will. Let’s see who really improvises and who sticks to a script.
